chose: A terminal card types its commands as a new design of the one card, terminal-v2, pinned by a new cheat-sheet version (v6 = v5 with terminal-v2), never by a per-line flag or a per-video switch. A line with a prompt shows the prompt, then types its keyword and text a character every 45 ms (about 22 a second) behind a steady block cursor that doesn't blink, then shows its comment. Every line appears at the time v1 gives it, so badges spell themselves out when the renderer counts them (BS1); a card where another line would appear while a command is still typing (its time plus 400 ms, 45 ms a character and 350 ms) is refused, naming the earliest atMs, so a command's output never shows before the command. The family is the cards' items appearing one at a time (cards.ts, `appearing` and `itemTimes`); typing is one way an item appears, kept in the terminal for now because only its lines are typed commands. A cheat sheet's or flow's command typed too would move the typing into cards.ts as a shared appearance, not copy it.
options: a new design, terminal-v2, pinned by a series version
move later lines until their command is typed (it breaks the renderer's badge timing, BS1)
gray: The owner asked for commands typed with the typewriter effect (#3476) and named no speed, cursor or what output does. Each is seen in every essay that pins v6, and a design is frozen once a published video uses it, so changing one later means another design.
undo: Pin cheat-sheet v5 (or a later version naming terminal-v1) in the essay; to change the look, add terminal-v3 and a series version naming it. terminal-v2 itself stays as drawn once a published video pins v6.
